analysis:
Examined the ClusterService.swift changes (patch, base lines 1-910). The change replaces cableMove with listenerChange, which now also detects pairing changes (.pairingChanged) and unpair (.unpaired) in addition to cable moves, and restarts the responder. It adds an injectable `Listening` struct (exchange port, control port, policy, selection) that defaults to production values (ClusterSetupLinkExchange.port/controlPort, .thunderboltOnly, selection read from context.linkSelection at each use). It also widens the visibility of `responder` and the check timestamps from private to internal.

Security-relevant observations: (1) The pairing-change detection is a hardening. Previously a listener stayed keyed with a stale edge secret after re-pairing. It now rekeys, or stops answering when unpaired. On .unpaired the responder is stopped and set to nil, and the guard that follows requires a valid pairing before a new responder is created, so a stale pairing key is not left answering. (2) Pairing store read errors return nil, which leaves the existing listener unchanged. That fails open with respect to the old key until the store is readable, but it is the same posture as before and not a regression. (3) The default policy remains thunderboltOnly, so there is no new network exposure in production. Only internal initializers can override ports or the policy, and the public convenience init does not pass `listening`. The Responder/Pairing.identity and cableMoved(bound:current:) signatures live in unseen files (ClusterSetupLinkExchange), so the new `Pairing.Identity` type and the `listener.pairing` and `listener.selection` properties were not verified. The controlResponder path (ensureControlResponder in ClusterServiceControl.swift) uses controlCheck and listening.controlPort, but those changes are outside this unit and were not seen. No impact on the provider/coordinator WebSocket, attestation, or inference-data assets. Threat IDs TB-002/T-053 are not affected. The next pass should confirm that the unseen Responder initializer enforces the policy and that the control listener applies the same pairing-change logic.
